title: Inference pathline metrics mapping and investigation notes
content:
Purpose:
This is a working doc to capture a compact mapping between user request pathlines (the logical journey a request takes through our stack) and the concrete metrics/traces we should create, surface on dashboards, and use during post-incident investigations for inference latency and correctness issues.

Scope / audience:
- Observability engineers, SREs, runtime engineers, and oncall.
- Focused on tokenized inference flows (streaming + non-streaming), multi-variant routing, and cache/batching interactions.

High-level idea (tl;dr):
- Treat each request as a pathline made of ordered anchors: http-entry -> router -> auth/quotas -> routing-decision -> allocator -> model-prepare (kv/cache load) -> kernel-run (batched op) -> response-stream-chunk -> post-processing.
- Instrument anchors with compact spans + stable tags (model, model_variant, seq_len_bucket, tenant_id, route, batch_id, kv_keyset_hash).
- Map each anchor to 1–3 metric primitives (timers, counters, ratios) and ensure SLI coverage for the user-facing path.

Metric definitions (working, names are suggestions):
- request.latency.total_ms: wall-time from http-entry -> response-stream-end (p50/p95/p99).
- request.latency.server_ms: http-entry -> kernel-run-end (excludes network/streaming).
- request.latency.tail_slice_{50,150,300,600}_ms: count of requests exceeding these thresholds, by model_variant.
- kv.cache.hit_rate: hits / (hits + misses) tagged by tenant, model_variant, and prefix_len_bucket.
- batching.avg_batch_size: avg number of sequences per kernel invocation, by model_variant and hour.
- batching.continuous_utilization_pct: proportion of kernel windows that were non-empty (proxy for wasted cycles).
- kernel.queue_wait_ms: time spent waiting in allocator queue before kernel launch.
- tokens.generated_per_request: counter of output tokens produced (useful for cost SLOs).
- fallback.router.count: number of times request rerouted to fallback model (tagged by reason: overload, mismatch, auth).
- errors.request_count and errors.kernel_oom_count (separate counters).
- cost.estimated_usd_per_1k: derived metric combining tokens.generated_per_request, model_variant price, and quantization flag.

Buckets and labels we rely on:
- seq_len_bucket: short (<=64), medium (65-512), long (>512).
- model_variant: base, quantized, lower-precision, ll2 (whatever we expose).
- tenant_tier: free, standard, dedicated.

Tracing anchors & span conventions (keep spans small, high cardinality tags only in logs):
- span.request.entry (tags: request_id, tenant_id, route, user_agent_short)
- span.router.decision (tags: model_variant, policy, fallback_flag)
- span.allocator.wait (tags: gpu_node_id, queue_reason)
- span.kv.load (tags: kv_keyset_hash, kv_hit: true/false)
- span.kernel.exec (tags: batch_id, batch_size, seq_len_bucket, quantization_profile)
- span.response.stream_chunk (tags: chunk_index, bytes)
Notes on sampling:
- Mandatory full traces for: requests that hit tail_slice_300_ms or higher, any request that triggers fallback.router, any kernel_oom, and periodic systematic 0.1% sampling for baselines.
- Severity-weighted reservoir sampling for partial traces (weight = max(1, latency_ms/100)). This preserves more high-latency traces without blowing up storage.

Dashboard wireframe notes (for the inference ops dashboard):
Top row (health):
- tiny KPI row: p50/p95/p99 total latency (global), kv.cache.hit_rate (global), batching.avg_batch_size (global), tail_slice_300_ms_count (24h).
Row 2 (breakdowns):
- heatmap: latency p95 by model_variant (rows) vs seq_len_bucket (cols) — color = p95 ms, hover shows sample traces and recent fallback count.
- sparkline panel per model_variant: cost.estimated_usd_per_1k and tokens.generated_per_min.
Row 3 (drilldowns):
- waterfall / timeline: selected request trace waterfall (render span durations stacked).
- top offenders table: top 50 request_ids by total latency last 2h with columns [request_id, tenant_id, model_variant, seq_len, batch_size, kv_hit(false)?, kernel_queue_ms].
Row 4 (operational controls):
- sampling controls toggle (increase trace sampling for a model_variant), cache debug toggle (force skip-cache to reproduce miss), replay link to run request in staging.

Investigation checklist (quick runbook for oncall):
1) Confirm user report: get example request_id/time or tenant and time range.
2) Query top offenders: pseudo-SQL -
   SELECT request_id, total_ms, model_variant, seq_len_bucket, batch_size FROM requests WHERE ts >= now()-2h ORDER BY total_ms DESC LIMIT 50;
3) Open 3 full traces (prefer different model_variants). Look at: allocator.wait vs kernel.exec, kv.load misses, and batch_size==1 pathological cases.
4) If kernel.exec dominated: check GPU metrics (util %, memory usage, kernel_latency_avg) and recent driver errors.
5) If allocator.wait dominated: check node capacity, pod/container placement skew, and batch sizing config.
6) If kv.load dominated: inspect kv_hotspotting (same prefix keys), increasing / decreasing prefix sharding, and verify local caching layer config.
7) If fallback.router triggered: check routing policy changes pushed recently, and available capacity for target variants.
8) Reproduce: use the replay tool with the exact headers (tenant, route, batching hints). Toggle cache and batching variables.
9) Create short postmortem note in incident channel with root-cause hypothesis and next action (scale, configuration change, model rollback).

Example queries & log grep snippets (pseudo):
- Top 10 tenants by tail requests:
  SELECT tenant_id, count(*) FROM requests WHERE total_ms > 300 GROUP BY tenant_id ORDER BY count DESC LIMIT 10;
- Detect tiny batches:
  SELECT model_variant, avg(batch_size) FROM kernel_invocations WHERE ts >= now()-1h GROUP BY model_variant HAVING avg(batch_size) < 2;
- KV hotspot check:
  SELECT kv_key_prefix, count(*) FROM kv_access WHERE ts >= now()-6h GROUP BY kv_key_prefix ORDER BY count DESC LIMIT 20;

Edge cases and gotchas (notes-to-self):
- High tail latency with normal p95 often means batching variability + long seqs occasionally bypassing batching windows. Look at batch size distribution, not just avg.
- Streaming responses can inflate apparent total_ms because client ACK/stream backpressure delays end-of-response timestamp. Provide server-only SLI for kernel latency.
- Avoid adding high-cardinality tags (full user IDs, request body hashes) to metrics; keep them as logs attached to traces only.

Open questions / next steps:
- Should we add a derived metric: request.latency.queued_ms_by_batch_size to correlate queue wait vs tiny batches? (proposal: INF-2345)
- Decide resource-level SLOs per tenant tier for kernel_queue_wait_ms — currently uninstrumented per-tenant.
- Explore adding a small local LRU for KV prefix shards to reduce cross-node miss storms. Need perf eval on tail latency.

Appendix: quick mapping table (anchor -> primary metric -> recommended alerts):
- http-entry -> request.latency.total_ms -> alert if p95 increases 2x vs baseline
- router.decision -> fallback.router.count -> alert on >5% fallback rate sustained 10m
- allocator.wait -> kernel.queue_wait_ms -> alert on p95 > 200ms for dedicated tenants
- kv.load -> kv.cache.hit_rate -> alert on drop >10% absolute in 5m window
- kernel.exec -> kernel.exec_ms p95 -> alert on p99 > configured threshold per model_variant

That's it for now — this is intentionally terse. Will iterate with visuals and a copy of the dashboard JSON once we prototype widgets.

Notes / provenance:
- Related ticket: INF-2345 (routing & batching anomalies)
- Design review scheduled: 2025-02-10 with runtime and SRE
- Slack thread: #obs-inference (see thread pinned messages)

-- Aisha
